recent_posts.title: Building a Responsive Tab Row in Jetpack Compose
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to build a ResponsiveTabRow component in Jetpack Compose that automatically chooses between TabRow and ScrollableTabRow based on content width. The tutorial demonstrates using SubcomposeLayout to measure tab content before rendering, ensuring tabs display correctly regardless of label length or localization. The implementation measures each tab's preferred width, compares it against available space, and selects the appropriate tab row type to prevent text cutoff or excessive empty space.

recent_posts.title: Exploring Jetpack Compose: ButtonGroup
recent_posts.summary: Material 3 Expressive introduces ButtonGroup, a new composable for displaying horizontal button collections with built-in animations and overflow handling. The component supports clickable buttons, single and multi-select toggles, and connected button groups (replacing deprecated segmented buttons). ButtonGroup automatically handles width animations through animateWidth modifier and MutableInteractionSource, expanding pressed buttons while compressing neighbors. The API provides helper functions (clickableItem, toggleableItem, customItem) within ButtonGroupScope, customizable expansion ratios, and overflow indicators. Connected button groups use specific shapes from ButtonGroupDefaults and can wrap across multiple lines with FlowRow. Currently experimental, requiring opt-in annotation.

recent_posts.title: How to configure Gemini effectively in Android Studio
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to optimize Gemini AI integration in Android Studio through eight practical steps: setting up API keys for expanded context windows, configuring agent rules and AGENTS.md files for project-specific instructions, managing context efficiently, leveraging image inputs for UI development, connecting MCP servers for external tool access, using file pickers for accurate references, and understanding when to use Agent versus Ask modes. These configurations help developers work more efficiently by providing better context to AI agents and reducing back-and-forth iterations.

recent_posts.title: Exploring Material 3 for Compose: Floating Action Button Menu
recent_posts.summary: Material 3 for Compose introduces FloatingActionButtonMenu, a new component that allows developers to create expandable floating action buttons with 2-6 related menu items. The component consists of three parts: FloatingActionButtonMenu (root container), ToggleFloatingActionButton (main button), and FloatingActionButtonMenuItem (individual menu items). This solution helps optimize screen space on mobile devices by consolidating multiple related actions into a single expandable interface, following Jetpack Compose's decoupled API principles.

recent_posts.title: Exploring Navigation 3 for Jetpack Compose
recent_posts.summary: Navigation 3 for Jetpack Compose introduces a simplified approach to app navigation by replacing navigation graphs with a back stack management system. Key features include automatic UI updates, scoped state retention, adaptive layouts, and parent-child communication. The new system allows developers to own and control the back stack directly, using serializable keys to represent destinations. Implementation involves setting up dependencies, defining destinations as data objects or classes, creating an entryProvider DSL for routing, and using the NavDisplay composable to render navigation content with automatic state management.

recent_posts.title: Exploring Material 3 for Compose: Large Top App Bar
recent_posts.summary: The LargeTopAppBar in Material 3 for Compose creates dynamic, scroll-responsive navigation that transitions between expanded and collapsed states based on user scrolling. It offers three scroll behaviors (enterAlways, exitUntilCollapsed, and pinned), supports navigation icons and actions, and allows customization of heights and colors. The component provides a more immersive user experience by adapting to user interaction while maintaining navigation context.

recent_posts.title: Material 3 Expressive for Compose: Loading Indicator
recent_posts.summary: Material 3 Expressive introduces new LoadingIndicator components for Jetpack Compose that animate between custom polygon shapes instead of traditional spinners. The LoadingIndicator and ContainedLoadingIndicator composables allow developers to create more engaging loading experiences by customizing colors, shapes, and animations using RoundedPolygon instances. This approach enables apps to incorporate unique branding elements while maintaining Material Design principles, offering a more expressive alternative to standard progress indicators.

recent_posts.title: Exploring Jetpack Compose for Widgets with Glance
recent_posts.summary: Jetpack Glance enables Android developers to create app widgets using Composables instead of RemoteViews. The tutorial covers the complete widget development process including setting up dependencies, creating GlanceAppWidget classes, composing UI with Glance-specific components, handling dependency injection with Hilt EntryPoints, implementing click actions with intents, and registering widgets in the manifest. The approach simplifies widget development while maintaining the limitations of AppWidgets and RemoteViews.

recent_posts.title: Exploring Jetpack Compose: DockedSearchBar
recent_posts.summary: Jetpack Compose's Material3 package provides a DockedSearchBar composable that offers a floating search bar, displaying selectable recommendations without consuming excessive space. This post explains how to implement and customize it, detailing essential properties like inputField and content for managing the search bar's state and behavior.

recent_posts.title: Exploring Jetpack Compose: SearchBar
recent_posts.summary: The post explains how to use the SearchBar composable provided by the Jetpack Compose Material3 package to implement a floating search bar in Android apps. It covers the key properties and customization options, including input field management and displaying recommendations. The post includes code examples demonstrating the implementation of the search bar and managing its expanded state to show recommendations.
